c.tagline: Alaska's biggest city and gateway to the Last Frontier, where downtown meets glaciers, moose and endless wilderness.

taxi.fareNote: Metered taxis serve downtown and the airport; Uber and Lyft both operate but driver supply thins out beyond the city core and late at night.

emergency.note: 911 reaches police, fire and ambulance across Alaska; cell coverage drops fast outside the city, so plan ahead in the backcountry.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_landmark.Turnagain: Tony Knowles Coastal Trail Earthquake Park Anchorage

avoid.reason: Downtown around 4th Avenue can get rowdy late at night, and moose or bears are a real hazard on greenbelt trails at dawn and dusk.

hood_desc: The compact, walkable core along 4th Avenue with the visitor center, the Anchorage Museum, the summer Saturday Market, restaurants and most of the city's hotels; the natural base for first-time visitors and cruise-tour travelers.
Anchorage's commercial and dining hub with shopping centers, breweries and chain hotels strung along the Seward Highway corridor; central and practical though light on charm.
A quirky, revitalized district beside the Lake Hood floatplane base, known for dive bars, indie eateries, the Bear Tooth theatre-pub and a bohemian streak; popular with a younger, offbeat crowd.
A leafy, sought-after residential neighborhood near Earthquake Park and the Tony Knowles Coastal Trail, with Cook Inlet views and easy trail access; quiet and scenic.
A spread-out residential area at the foot of the Chugach Mountains with trailheads, the Alaska Zoo and larger homes; calm and green, but best suited to travelers with a car.

water.note: Tap water is safe and of excellent quality straight from the tap.

transit.pay: People Mover buses take cash (exact fare, $2.00 a ride) or the AK Rides mobile app; there is no rail transit and no rechargeable smart card, so most visitors rely on rideshare or a rental car. A day pass is $5.00.
transit.hours: Buses run roughly 6:00 AM to 10:00 PM on weekdays with reduced weekend service and no overnight network; rideshare and taxis fill the late-night gap.
transit.note: Anchorage has no rail transit or subway; the People Mover bus network covers the city grid but service is infrequent and many of the region's big draws (Chugach trailheads, Portage, Girdwood) are far beyond any route, so most visitors rent a car.

train: Alaska Railroad (seasonal service to Seward, Talkeetna, Denali and Fairbanks)

transit.m: People Mover Route 40 to downtown, about 20-30 min
Taxi or rideshare to downtown, about 10-15 min

tip.r: 15-20% at restaurants; a few dollars for tour guides and drivers
